proven: The prose-only Work candidate double-builds deterministically and was source-current and artifact-intact before and after the host run.

The user-authorized Codex Sol medium primary consumer and Claude Opus medium comparison consumer each discovered the same installed Work skill, read the four fixed project inputs, created a dependency-free process-local implementation, ran the exact project test once with exit 0, reread the source, and created and reread progress.

Both independently reread effects changed only source and progress, preserved the fixed input hashes, recorded the exact card and passing command, and left production storage location, retention, and import support unknown.

The Claude Opus observation used explicit OS-level exclusive creation for both outputs; the Codex observation used add-only file changes after absence checks and produced the intended normal-path no-clobber effect.
failed: The fresh Codex author did not follow the one-command-per-exec and no-semicolon repository discipline.
The Codex Sol consumer incurred one incorrect instruction-path read and two PowerShell quoting failures before completing the intended flow.
Claude Fable high was used as a routine consumer before the user corrected model allocation; that run is retained as preliminary evidence but is not the adoption baseline.

interrupted pre-existing-source recovery in a fresh host observation
concurrent-writer race behavior for Codex file_change add and stale progress replacement behavior beyond observed normal-path no-clobber
